name: Framework Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Framework Ventures (framework.ventures; adviser entity Framework Ventures Management, LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser per its disclosures page), the San Francisco VC founded in 2019 by Vance Spencer and Michael Anderson. It made its name as an early crypto/DeFi investor (Aave, Chainlink) and since its June 2026 Fund IV also backs AI, physical AI and robotics, fintech and energy. Fortune and Cointelegraph (June 2026) match the founders, city and fund history. Not Framework Computer (the laptop maker) and not Framework Venture Partners or other similarly named funds.

open_items: Fund I: size and close date not published. The site says the firm was founded in 2019 and has 'four funds'; Cointelegraph says it launched its first crypto fund in 2019. Fund II-IV dates are announcement dates (WSJ 2021-05-14 per the about page; Bloomberg April 2022; Fortune 2026-06-26), not verified final closes.

SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent, so Form D filings (fund legal names, exact sizes, dates) were not checked. Fortune cites an SEC filing showing $1.28B AUM in December 2025 (not recorded as a fund).
No application form or apply URL. The contact page lists only a general 'for founders' inbox (address not recorded), so accepts_cold_inbound = yes is inferred from it.

requires_us_entity = no is inferred, not stated: the investments list (as of June 16, 2026) includes non-US entities such as Singapore Pte. Ltd., Finnish Oy, Australian Pty Ltd and UK Ltd companies. Nothing found on investing in Indian founders.

portfolio_count_reported not stated. The investments list has about 108 entity names (excluding undisclosed and written-off deals) and the Getro job board shows 62 companies; neither is a reported count.
Stages: the firm says only 'early-stage'; seed and Series A are mapped from that and the rounds found. It also led a pre-seed (Unto Labs).

Stated sectors: the firm names 'AI', 'physical AI and robotics', 'fintech'/'financial services', 'infrastructure' and (via Fortune) 'energy'. Mapping generic 'AI' and 'infrastructure' to ai_apps_agents and ai_infra is our classification.

Not recorded: Framework's ~$45M (~10%) stake in public mortgage lender Better and a $500M financing partnership via the Sky stablecoin ecosystem (Cointelegraph citing Fortune; public company, no deal page read); Obex (Forbes, Nov 2025, 403); Antimetal (Framework-led 2023 seed appears only in database hits; the Built In page on its 2025 $20M Series A does not name Framework); Daylight's Business Wire release (403) and its earlier a16z-led round; Blockworks coverage of Meanwhile (403).

Valuations reported but not recorded as post-money because the press doesn't say pre or post: Meanwhile 'values Meanwhile at $190 million'; Unto Labs 'values the San Francisco-based company at $140 million'.
Company websites, HQ and founding year are missing for several rounds (Ultra, Mecka AI, Midas, Daylight, Perle, Plasma, Glow, Meanwhile). Framework's own headline calls Ultra 'Ultra Robotics'.
Mecka AI: the $60M combines a $25M Series A (closed November 2025) and a $35M follow-on, both led by Framework; Fortune doesn't split the participants between them.

Partners: focus_sectors are classified from team-page bios and deal quotes; the firm assigns no sector coverage. Nick Trileski has no LinkedIn link on the site. Ben Floyd's caption says 'Partner' but his bio says 'Venture Partner' (New York). Adam Badrawi (Partner, Head of IR & Global Comms) left out as non-investing.
